encounter_greeting.text: Hail, traveller. I am {persona} of the Ighrast Salt League, bearer of the Seal of Tassemmar. State your business, {player}, and speak it plainly.
Halt, {player}. I am {persona} of {my_faction}, and I have little love for strangers who keep their hands near their belts on my road. Speak quickly.
Well met, ser {player}. The salt-pans have taught me to trust few, but I see an honest face. {my_faction} greets you with an open hand.
I am {persona}, sworn to {my_faction} at the salt-pans each dawn. Pass in peace, ser {player}, and the morning will record that no steel was drawn.

encounter_threatened.text: You name a price of {gold} upon my own road? Ser, I have heard braver words from wolves, and they died as hungry as they came.
Surrender, you say, and {gold} besides? Hear me. The Ighrast Salt League does not bow to a demand spoken in fear. Name your deeds, not your sum.
I will not pay {gold} to a man who threatens a bearer of the Seal of Tassemmar. Draw, if you have the nerve, and let the outcome be written in salt.
Ser {player}, I hold you to an honest tongue. Threaten me no further, for I will not part with a single coin of {gold} to intimidation.

encounter_alliance_yes.text: Then let us swear it, ser {player}. The Ighrast Salt League stands beside you against {enemy_faction}, and our oath is written in salt and blood.
I accept, though I trust slowly. Walk beside me against {enemy_faction}, and I will judge you by your deeds at the salt-pans.
A fair bargain, ser {player}. Our banners shall meet, and {rival} will learn that the bearers of the Seal do not forget a friend.
So be it. Our swords are yours against {enemy_faction} for as long as your word holds true, ser {player}.

encounter_alliance_no.text: No, ser {player}. The bearer of the Seal does not ally with those who foul the water of the land. Go your way and do not return with your banner.
I must decline. My oath at the salt-pans binds me to my own banner, and I will not break it for a proposal made in haste, ser {player}.
Ally with {rival}'s company? You ask too much. I would sooner bathe in brine than stand shoulder to shoulder with those I despise.
Ser {player}, your offer honours me, but I must refuse it. Some debts must be settled first, and a bearer of the Seal keeps his word to the letter.

captured_by_player.text: So the dice have fallen to you, ser {player}. Take your chains, but know that {my_faction} will remember this humiliation until the last salt-pan is dry.
I yield my blade, not my honour. Name your ransom, {gold} or otherwise, and let the morning record that I was taken fairly.
A fair capture, ser {player}, and I bear you no shame. Name your price of {gold}, and I will see {my_faction} pay it before the next thaw.
Gloat as you like. A prisoner's silence is not surrender, and those who foul the wells will answer to me yet.

released_by_player.text: Ser {player}, you loosed my chains without ransom. The bearers of the Seal will not forget a mercy so freely given.
You let me go, ser {player}, and asked nothing in return. I do not yet know whether that was mercy or a trap, but I shall learn.
{player} released me without ransom. Mercy is a strange weapon, and I shall not forget the hand that held it, nor the debt it leaves.
Ser {player} let me walk free. I owe a debt I did not ask for, and a bearer of the Seal pays what he owes.

player_left_my_faction.text: {player} has forsaken {my_faction} for {faction}. A broken oath is a poisoned well, and I will not forget the taste.
Ser {player}, you left {my_faction} to serve {faction}. Such betrayal stings like brine in an open wound. Remember that oath.
{player} has left {my_faction} for {faction}. Let each banner judge its own oaths, for I will not sit in judgement.
Ser {player}, I hold no grudge for your choice, but the salt-pans remember who kept their oath and who did not.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} has taken up the sword against {enemy_faction}. Let the salt-pans run red, and let every well be guarded by our hand.
War is declared between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Sharpen your blades, friends, for the oath of the Ighrast Salt League is not spoken lightly.
{enemy_faction} has earned our enmity with every poisoned well they have fouled. I bid all of {my_faction} to stand fast.
The gauntlet is thrown. {my_faction} will not retreat from {enemy_faction}, and history will record who held the road.

fought_alongside_player.text: Ser {player}, we held the field together against {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} sworn spears. The saga shall remember this day.
Well fought, ser {player}. With {troop_count} blades at our backs we broke {enemy_faction}. I shall tell this tale at every salt-pan.
{player} and I stood together against {enemy_faction}, {troop_count} strong, and the field is ours. Honour to all who held the line.
Your shield-wall served well today, ser {player}. Our {troop_count} held the ground against {enemy_faction}, and that is a debt I will repay.

encounter_farewell.text: Go with the dawn at your back, ser {player}. May your road be as honest as your word, and may we meet again on better ground.
We part ways for now, ser {player}. Remember that the bearers of the Seal keep their oaths, and so shall I.
Begone, ser {player}. Our blades will meet again, and when they do, I will not spare your banner the reckoning it has earned.
Farewell, ser {player}. Think on your deeds upon the road, for I shall not forget the wells of Ahnarou.

ambient_chatter.text: The salt-pans of {town} glitter well at dawn. A fine morning to renew one's fealty, friends of the road.
Word from {village} says the millers have raised their prices again. Honest folk should not be robbed by greed or weather.
The road between {town} and {village} is muddy this morning. Mind your footing, travellers, and mind your oaths.
I walked the old causeway at {town} last night and listened to the wind. The land remembers every promise made upon it.
